title: GIRAFFE: Representing Scenes as Compositional Generative Neural Feature Fields
abstract:
*CVPR 2021 Best Paper*

## Motivation

- Controllable Generation of Images (Scenes)
- Incorporating 3D representations into 2D image synthesis task
- Employing compositional nature of visual scenes

## Key Idea

- Encode each object as 3D Neural Radiance Field(NeRF)
- Combine them using weighted volume density average
- Volume render objects after affine transformation into the scene space (Object space --> Scene space)
- 2D render 3D representation using normal CNN

## Previous Approach

- NeRF: One network (MLP) for one scene
- GRAF: Direct translation into 2D RGB space

## Comments

- The idea of employing 3D compositional nature of visual scenes is very appealing, and I definitely agree that this is the right way to be headed even when we are dealing with 2D RGB domains.
- Incorporating 3D neural implicit representations gave great capacity for disentanglement and controllability especially in 3D features like camera angle and rotation.
- However, the evaluation fell a bit short for its theory and motivations, as they mostly used iconic datasets; samples mostly had one main object in the center, so **GIRAFFE*'s compositional design could not be thoroughly inspected.
- Datasets like CelebA and LSUN are rather very easy, so it may be waste of compute to learn 3D representations for such rather simple and straight-forward tasks.
